headline: Subscription growth and cost discipline lift profit
summary_short: Revenue rose 6% year-over-year to $657.0 million as operating income grew 36% to $50.3 million and diluted EPS more than tripled to $0.45, while cash fell to $111.5 million following debt-refinancing activity.
summary_long: Revenue grew 6% y/y to $657.0 million on subscription growth from new customers and AI-led upsell; gross margin held near 72% despite higher infrastructure costs. Operating income rose 36% to $50.3 million as revenue outpaced R&D, sales, and G&A growth. Net income climbed to $39.1 million, aided by a $15.0 million gain from an amended Avaya agreement. Cash fell to $111.5 million after settling $609.1 million of convertible notes, drawing $600.0 million on the Term Loan, and repurchasing $175.0 million of stock in H1. Dividend held flat at $0.075/share. The 10-Q states no forward guidance.

drivers.explanation: Subscriptions revenue increased 6% y/y, primarily due to acquisition of new customers and upsell of products, including new AI-led products.
Gross margin held near 72% as a $10.2 million rise in infrastructure support costs was largely offset by a $1.9 million decrease in third-party support costs.
Operating income grew as 6% revenue growth outpaced combined R&D (+7%), sales and marketing (+4%), and G&A (+2%) expense growth.
Tracks the operating-income improvement described above, plus steady depreciation and amortization.
Net income rose on higher operating income plus a $15.0 million gain recognized from an amended agreement with partner Avaya, booked in other income.
Follows net income growth, further boosted by a lower diluted share count after continued buybacks.
Cash fell as $609.1 million used to settle maturing 2026 Convertible Notes and $175.0 million of H1 stock repurchases outpaced $600.0 million drawn under the new Term Loan.
Long-term debt rose as $600.0 million was drawn under the Term Loan to help fund settlement of the maturing 2026 Convertible Notes, which had been classified as a current liability.
The equity deficit widened as $175.0 million of H1 share repurchases exceeded H1 net income of $69.7 million.
Held at $0.075/share, the same rate declared in Q1 2026, the quarter the company initiated its inaugural dividend payout.
MD&A frames the quarter as continued growth from new-customer acquisition and AI-led product upsell, with expense growth held below revenue growth across R&D, sales, and G&A.
